markdown_report:
At 0% progress, prioritize a small, testable change: **recent-evidence gated SASRec**, targeting stale-interest influence and broadly related recommendations that crowd out specific recent matches. Improvement remains a hypothesis until measured by pinned macro validation HR@10.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) SASRec can attend across the history. However, attention alone does not require repeated recent evidence to outweigh incidental older interactions. (2) Electronics has 14.95% negative-over-positive positions and a −0.4812 lower-tail margin. These identify ranking confusion, but do not establish its cause or validation performance. (3) Embedding similarity scores lie near the zero-cosine reference. Strong collapse is therefore a weak justification for adding diversity regularization.

**Insights from related work.** (1) [TLSTSRec](https://doi.org/10.3233/IDA-240051) motivates adaptive long/short-term fusion. This supports testing an explicit recent-intent branch without replacing SASRec. (2) [gSASRec](https://www.ijcai.org/proceedings/2024/0939.pdf) addresses negative-sampling overconfidence through multiple negatives and generalized BCE. It provides an objective-level alternative, rather than evidence that architecture causes the observed confusion. (3) [SComGNN](https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.02130) distinguishes complementary relations from generic similarity. It motivates directional evidence, although observed purchase transitions cannot establish compatibility or complementarity.

The resulting directions are temporal evidence selection, ranking-objective calibration, and directional relation modeling.

| Direction | Minimal experiment | Principal uncertainty |
|---|---|---|
| Temporal selection | Recent-evidence gate | Recent activity may be incidental |
| Objective calibration | 128-negative gBCE | Training separation may not transfer |
| Directional relations | Training-transition residual | Sparse transitions may be noisy |

Scores below use originality/potential/user alignment/model alignment/difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

1. **Recent-evidence gate: 4/7/8/7/4.** Originality: explicit evidence weighting, but established fusion family. Potential: reusable intent control, but sparse histories weaken it. User alignment: addresses stale influence and broad-match crowding, but cannot verify prerequisites. Model alignment: may resolve confusing contexts, but margins could remain unchanged. Difficulty: small branch, but causal masking needs care.
2. **128-negative gBCE: 2/8/4/9/3.** Originality: new benchmark application, but established method. Potential: scalable objective improvement, but uncertain transfer. User alignment: sharper competition, but no direct intent mechanism. Model alignment: targets sampled ranking behavior, but diagnostics do not establish sampling bias. Difficulty: localized loss change, but increased memory.
3. **Directed transition residual: 5/6/7/6/5.** Originality: separates directional evidence, but graph precedents exist. Potential: useful complements, but weak transition coverage. User alignment: supports next-choice evidence, but cannot confirm compatibility. Model alignment: adds discriminative signals, but can amplify popularity. Difficulty: sparse implementation, but additional inference artifacts.

Select idea 1. Fuse SASRec features with a recent-window representation whose weights increase with repeated semantic evidence in the observed prefix. Learn a conservative gate. This explicitly targets older/incidental influence and broad relatedness displacing recent specific interests; sharper context targets the measured ranking confusion. Preserve splits, seeds, routing, and baseline loss. Compare backbone, recent-only, fixed fusion, and learned fusion under the shared budget; select exclusively by four-category macro validation HR@10.

idea.description: Add a causal recent-intent branch to each category's SASRec and learn a conservative gate between its representation and the backbone representation. Weight recent items using agreement with other observed prefix items, providing a soft proxy for repeated interests without requiring exact repeat purchases.
idea.motivation: The user diagnosis identifies two directly targeted failures: occasional or older interactions outweigh repeated recent interests, and broadly related items crowd out specific recent matches. Recent evidence supplies an explicit alternative to unrestricted history attention. The model-facing target is positive–negative confusion, particularly Electronics' 14.95% wrong-rank rate. Neither diagnostic establishes that this change will improve validation HR@10.
idea.implementation_notes: Keep category-specific models, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], and the environment epoch default of 200. Start with a five-item recent window. For each recent item, compute repetition support as the mean positive cosine similarity to other items in the causal prefix; exclude its own position and padding. Detach these support weights initially to reduce feedback toward artificially similar embeddings. Softmax the support scores within the recent window and pool item embeddings. Normalize and project the pool to the SASRec feature dimension. A scalar sigmoid gate conditioned on backbone features, recent features, their cosine agreement, and log prefix length controls their mixture; initialize its bias to -2 to favor the backbone. Retain the baseline loss and negative sampler to isolate the architecture change. Exact repeats may be rare, so semantic support is only a learned proxy and cannot establish equipment compatibility or satisfied demand. Update the predictor writer to emit the identical architecture and checkpoint configuration, keeping artifacts beneath the trial directory. Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device).run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions; expose the actual module through view.model, fused features through log2feats, and unchanged candidate scoring through predict_score. Do not use unavailable ratings, reviews, categories, prices, stores, or simulator traits. Report masked causal margin diagnostics and embedding similarity with their definitions; omit unavailable category breakdowns explicitly. Evaluate ablations only within the shared GPU budget and select using the pinned macro validation HR@10.
idea.pseudocode:
For every valid training position t:
    prefix = sequence[:t+1]
    h = SASRec(prefix)[-1]
    recent = last min(5, len(prefix)) valid positions
    for j in recent:
        support[j] = mean(max(0, cosine(E[j], E[k]))) over k in prefix, k != j
        use zero support when there is no other valid position
    weights = softmax(stop_gradient(support))
    r = LayerNorm(project(sum_j weights[j] * E[j]))
    g = sigmoid(MLP(concat(h, r, cosine(h,r), log1p(prefix_length))))
    z = LayerNorm((1-g)*h + g*r)
    score positive and sampled negative items using z and candidate embeddings
    optimize the unchanged baseline objective
Vectorize with causal masks or prefix accumulations; do not materialize an unrestricted B x L x L x D tensor.
At inference, apply the identical computation to the final observed position.
Select checkpoints and variants using pinned four-category macro validation HR@10.

originality.positive: Adds an explicit repeated-evidence signal to a small recent-intent gate, making the proposed behavior directly testable.
originality.negative: Long/short-term fusion and learned gating are established; this is an incremental adaptation.

future_potential.positive: Provides a compact framework for testing when recent repeated evidence should control sequential recommendations.
future_potential.negative: Learned semantic agreement may reflect popularity or broad similarity rather than a specific user purpose.

code_difficulty.positive: Retains the backbone, objective, data pipeline, and item scoring interface.
code_difficulty.negative: Requires careful causal support computation, predictor serialization, and diagnostic compatibility.

related_work.title: Self-Attentive Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Uses causal self-attention to encode interaction histories for next-item scoring.
limitations: Its architecture does not explicitly require repeated recent evidence to dominate incidental older interactions.

related_work.title: TLSTSRec
contributions: Combines temporal information with adaptive long/short-term preference fusion.
limitations: The supplied evidence does not establish gains under the pinned four-category RecHarness evaluation.

related_work.title: gSASRec
contributions: Uses multiple negatives and generalized BCE to correct sampling-induced overconfidence.
limitations: Does not directly encode recent intent, compatibility, or whether a purchase satisfied a need.
The provided diagnostics do not establish sampling bias as the cause of benchmark errors.

related_work.title: SComGNN
contributions: Models complementary relations using low-pass and mid-pass graph filters, distinguishing complementarity from generic similarity.
limitations: Successive public interactions do not establish complementarity or product compatibility.
Its reported results do not demonstrate improvement on this benchmark.
